messages:
incident-bot: Pager: P1 reported by HeliosTech — elevated 502/503s for requests from their VPC private deployment behind our NLB. Alerting channel and paging oncall. See logs: request spikes + target health fails.
jamie (oncall): I'm on it. key details? HeliosTech says ~40% of requests failing, started ~08:12 UTC.
anita (customer-eng): customer slack says errors from app origin, all regions but specific to their private VPC via NLB. They tried restart, no change.
lee (sre): Looking at NLB target groups for their tenant pool now. Running curl from control-plane into their VPC shows 502. NLB healthcheck showing 504/timeout to targets.
sofia (netops): Can you paste the NLB target IPs? I'll check VPC route tables and SGs. Might be egress ACL or new security group rule.
jamie (oncall): Target IPs: 10.2.45.12, 10.2.45.13, 10.2.45.14 (tenant pool). Healthcheck config: /healthz, 5s interval, 2s timeout.
lee (sre): I grabbed the NLB logs — lots of connection resets. Backend connections failing TLS handshake in some traces. Attaching sample snippet:```nlb-log: client=10.10.5.3 backend=10.2.45.12 code=502 proto=HTTP/1.1 conn=reset```
sofia (netops): Running VPC flow logs: I see a flood of SYN followed by RST from the backends around 08:11-08:18. No recent SG edits logged in the audit API for that subnet.
mike (edge): Edge telemetry shows increase in header size for HeliosTech calls (long cookie blobs). Could be pushing slow start on backend. Is there any rate-limiting rule on their tenant pool?
jamie (oncall): Not on platform side, we do have per-tenant conn limits — but quota is well under.
sofia (netops): I quickly checked route table: NAT gateway healthy. But I do see a transient spike of ICMP frag needed from one backend; MTU mismatch possibility?
lee (sre): Hmm. Also seeing repeated TLS renegotiation failures with backend process logs: "handshake: alert handshake_failure". Could be a cert expiry or ciphers mismatch.
anita (customer-eng): HeliosTech confirms they rolled app side TLS config yesterday (rotated certs). Could be an incompat change.
jamie (oncall): Immediate mitigation options: 1) failover NLB traffic to a previous-compatible pool variant (v1) 2) open temporary passthrough to bypass ALB layer (if present) 3) coordinate with customer to rollback TLS rotation. Thoughts?
sofia (netops): We can add a weighted route to redirect 100% -> dedicated fallback pool that we control (same region) in ~5min. Need approval to adjust routing policy.
mike (edge): Fallback pool has capacity and compatible TLS config. I can update routing policy and healthcheck config to be slightly more lenient. Expect cutover ~4-6min and can observe for errors.
lee (sre): Before failover, let's try a quick NLB connection debug: exec into one healthy control-plane VM in their VPC and run `openssl s_client -connect 10.2.45.12:443 -servername <host>` to see handshake details. If it's cert mismatch from Helios side, that will show.
jamie (oncall): I'll try the openssl test and post results.
jamie (oncall): openssl shows: "SSL_connect: SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL in connection to 10.2.45.12:443" and server sends TLS alert (handshake_failure). Looks consistent with Helios rotated config.
anita (customer-eng): I pinged Helios PM — they're reverting rotation now. ETA 12 minutes. They asked for our workaround because revert might not be instant.
sofia (netops): Given revert ETA, I recommend we do a partial failover 50/50 to fallback pool so customer traffic is preserved while we validate. Lower blast radius.
mike (edge): Doing 50% weighted shift now to fallback pool; changing routing policy in control-plane. Will post when complete.
deploy-bot: Route change triggered by mike at 08:25 UTC; plan id r-6b2f.
mike (edge): 50% -> fallback applied, backends show healthy, error rate dropped to ~8% within 90s.
lee (sre): Observed application logs for HeliosTech on fallback show successful TLS handshakes. NLB metrics confirm reduced 502/503 on customer LB.
anita (customer-eng): Helios confirmed seeing less errors on their end for some tenants. They will continue revert and test.
jamie (oncall): I'm going to monitor for 30 min. If Helios completes revert, we'll gradually shift 100% back. If not, we keep fallback. Documenting actions for postmortem.
sofia (netops): Added temporary firewall exception to allow larger MTU probes for diagnostic frames (no change to production policy).
lee (sre): Creating incident runbook note: possible cause = client-side TLS rotation incompatible with backend ciphers; mitigation = weighted failover to platform-managed fallback pool.
anita (customer-eng): I'll coordinate with Helios PM and schedule a joint postmortem call.
jamie (oncall): Handoff to lee for overnight monitoring. I'm leaving the channel. @lee take it. :white_check_mark:
lee (sre): Acknowledged. I'll keep watch and escalate if error rate >5% for 15m. Logging timeline + metrics snapshot to the incident ticket.
incident-bot: Incident closed in channel — oncall handoff recorded. Severity downgraded after mitigation and customer partial revert.
